While I do agree, these things DO NOT confirm HL3, I feel that it IS still happening.

Here is why:

Look at the history of HL related leaks. In 2011, there were a lot of leaks. A LOT. In 2012, there were only a few, and since then, it has dropped to ~one leak a year, maybe two. I think that after 2011, someone started watching everything going out for HL leaks, and tries to prevent it happening.

We were getting leaks in things relating to Source 2. Source 2 has matured now. It is no longer in an Alpha state, it is at least Beta. Dota 2 is developing a fairly complete game using it. Previously in Alpha, the engine was progressing so quickly that everyone used one version of the engine. This was the point where every team was working on it and saying "Hey, feature X would be useful to have in the engine!" Since the engine has reached "Beta," and is almost (or completely) feature complete, everyone has started using their own "branch" of Source 2 for their project. Valve used to use one version of the engine for all the games, such as in the Orange box. Since then, however, Valve has changed that. Every game has its own engine version, all based off a common core, IE "Source SDK 2013" (or whatever internal version they use). Look at the Portal 2 engine: it has removed the code that enables you to have other people in the game, hence the Portal Stores: Mel devs having to play some clever tricks to get human NPCs in the game. I think that since Source 2 is "feature complete," the game devs have all split off and started working on their own branches, or branches shared between games that are similar. (Like Counterstrike Source 2 Edition, Left for Dead 3, Half Life 3, and possibly Team Fortress 2: Source 2 Port would use one "branch" of the engine designed for a first person shooter, while Dota 2 uses a branch designed more for a top-down game.) Each "branch" of the game is then "forked" to add game specific features (Like the Portal gun, Gravity gun, competetive matchmaking, etc). The reason we aren't seeing any more leaks in Dota 2 code is that they are not working in the same "branch" of the engine as Half Life 3, and other FPS games being developed inside of Valve. While improvements to the engine that aren't game specific are sent "upstream" from each game, they go through code review to keep references to specific games out to keep them secret/keep the base engine less game-specific (Unlike the original Source which was heavily tied into Half Life 2 until after the Orange Box. Look at GMod before it got its own Source version. Even if you just had TF2, you got all the textures and models from Half Life 2.)

Another reason for the tightened security around the game is that they don't want a repeat of 2003. They had the game all ready to go, got hacked, and had to delay the game. If you look at a lot of the tours with pictures taken inside Valve HQ, there is always the secret room/secret floor they couldn't visit because secret stuff was happening. I think this is where things like Half Life 3 and/or Left 4 Dead 3 are being worked on. Stuff that they are working on but don't want anyone to see. Nobody sees it, nobody knows it exists or any info about it, it is harder for someone to steal anything related to it. This is also why they have cut down on things "accidentally" getting leaked in game files, pictures, etc. They want their project, whatever it is, be it L4D3 or HL3 or something else, to remain secret until they are ready to launch it. I think this may also explain the sudden radio silence surrounding Half Life 3, at least coming from Valve. Little things were popping up all over the place as they didn't know what they were doing. In 2011/2012, after Portal 2, someone got an idea and started working on it. They cracked down on leaks, and started to get to work. The game has been in development for the past 3 years, the team working on whatever is needed (Creating Source 2, writing the story, assets, etc) and as of more recently the game has been under heavier development. They don't want anything getting leaked, and so security is tight.
